primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic syndrome–driven cardiometabolic disease with hypertension, prediabetes, early CKD and obesity

medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 – ACE‑I first‑line for hypertension and CKD

medications.dose: 500 mg once daily with evening meal, titrate by 500 mg weekly to 1000 mg twice daily (target 2000 mg/day)
medications.purpose: Prediabetes / early type‑2 diabetes glucose control
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 – Metformin first‑line for pre‑diabetes/diabetes

medications.dose: 10 mg once daily (if eGFR ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m²; 5 mg if eGFR 30‑44)
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular and renal protection (HF/CKD risk reduction)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 & NG28 – SGLT2‑i first‑line for HFrEF and CKD regardless of diabetes status
NICE CG181 – Statin for primary prevention when QRISK ≥10 % or metabolic syndrome present

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily (increase to 10 mg after 2 weeks if needed)
medications.duration: Until BP <140/90 mmHg achieved, then review
medications.purpose: Additional antihypertensive if target not met after ACE‑I optimisation
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 – CCB second‑line antihypertensive, glucose‑neutral

medications.dose: 1 g up to 3 g per day (max 4 g if renal function stable)
medications.duration: As needed – review pain control regularly
medications.nice_justification: NICE guidance on analgesia in chronic pain – avoid NSAIDs in CKD

medications.dose: 25 mg once daily, titrate to 100 mg daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Until migraine frequency reduced, then review
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG150 – Topiramate recommended for migraine prevention

interactions_checked.interaction: Risk of hyperkalaemia with ACE‑I in setting of borderline high potassium
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum K⁺ 1‑2 weeks after any dose change; avoid adding potassium‑sparing diuretics

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering may cause symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start dapagliflozin at low dose, re‑check BP after 1‑2 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined glucose‑lowering increases risk of euglycaemic DKA
interactions_checked.action: Educate on sick‑day rules, advise hydration, stop SGLT2‑i if acutely ill

interactions_checked.interaction: ACE‑I may modestly increase statin plasma levels
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin (lower interaction risk) and monitor CK/LFTs

contraindications.reason: CKD (creatinine 1.4 mg/dL) and hypertension – NSAIDs worsen renal function and fluid retention
Fluid retention risk and contraindicated in CKD/heart failure
Negative inotrope – contraindicated in heart failure per NG106
Negative inotrope – contraindicated in heart failure per NG106
Can worsen glucose tolerance and electrolyte balance in CKD
contraindications.alternative: Low‑dose thiazide only if needed after specialist review

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m²; must be confirmed before initiating metformin and dapagliflozin and dose‑adjusted if <45 mL/min.
QRISK score not available – assumed ≥10 % given hypertension, obesity, prediabetes; calculate formally before statin initiation.
Liver function tests not recorded – obtain baseline LFTs prior to starting atorvastatin.
Allergy history not documented – verify no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statins, or sulfonamides before prescribing.
Exact BMI not recorded – assumed ≥30 kg/m² based on obesity flag; consider GLP‑1 RA if weight loss needed after first‑line therapy.
Current analgesic use not detailed – assumed possible NSAID use; replace with paracetamol as advised.
treatment_summary: Continue lisinopril for hypertension and renal protection, add metformin MR and dapagliflozin for glucose control and cardiometabolic protection, start atorvastatin for primary CVD prevention, and consider low‑dose amlodipine if BP remains above target. Replace NSAIDs with paracetamol for pain and introduce topiramate for migraine prophylaxis. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, potassium, blood pressure, HbA1c, lipid profile, and liver enzymes at recommended intervals. Address data gaps (eGFR, QRISK, LFTs, allergies) before finalising therapy.
